t: Iran war: first session after the US–Israeli strikes
how: The strikes began on Saturday 28 Feb. Brent rose 10–13% to about $80–82; the Dow fell over 400 points and the S&P 500 0.7%.

t: S&P 500 low of the war sell-off: 6,316.91
how: Brent was near $118 and the Nasdaq had closed in correction during March. The index rose 17.3% from this low to 24 July.

t: Iran ceasefire: oil’s largest one-day fall since 2020
how: The ceasefire was announced late on 7 Apr. Brent fell over 13% to $94.75. The stock index move that day was not found.

t: Chip rout and strong jobs report: Nasdaq −4.18%
how: S&P 500 −2.64% to 7,383.74; a chip fund fell 10%, its worst day since March 2020. Odds of a rate rise by year-end jumped to 73% from 51%. The index made new highs afterwards.

t: US–Iran memorandum signed; Warsh’s first Fed meeting holds
how: Brent had fallen under $80 the day before. Oil kept falling for two weeks and stocks rose into late July.

t: Semiconductor index makes its closing high for the year
how: No news marked the day. The index was 42.5% lower by 20 Nov; the S&P 500 went on rising for another 15 weeks.

t: US crude closes under $70 as tankers pass Hormuz
how: Oil fell 4%; WTI at $69.63 was below $70 for the first time since 2 March. The summer low was $68.58 on 1 July.

t: Trump declares the Iran memorandum “over”
how: Brent jumped to $78.02 from $71.57 a week earlier and Iran said the strait was closed again. The S&P 500 was still higher two weeks later.

t: Brent back above $100 after tanker strikes
how: First close above $100 since 26 May. The S&P 500 closed at 7,411.98 the next day, 17.3% above its March low.

t: Fed holds 9–3; three officials vote for a rate rise
how: Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissented in favour of raising. The index move that day was not found.

t: Dow Jones record close
how: The Dow did not regain this level and was 11.4% lower on 20 Nov. The S&P 500 made new highs for two more months.

t: Small caps, mid caps and industrials make their highs
how: The Russell 2000 was 15.9% lower by 20 Nov. A narrower group of stocks carried the S&P 500 to its October record.

t: Brent closes above $100 and stays there
how: US–Iran fighting escalated; Brent $101.21. Diesel hit a record $6.06 two days later and the odds of a September rate rise passed 90%.

t: 10-year Treasury yield touches 5%
how: First time since 2023, with crude above $108 the same day. The 2-year yield stood far above the policy rate; the bond sell-off was described as orderly.

t: Fed raises rates to 3.75–4.00%, the first rise since 2023
how: Stocks turned down during the press conference: S&P 500 −0.45% to 7,551.81, large banks −3% to −4%. The index was at a record three weeks later.

t: G7 to release 100m barrels of crude and diesel
how: Brent stayed above $100. The VIX closed at 15.31, close to its low for the autumn.

t: S&P 500 record close: 7,818.93
how: Up 0.58%, led by chipmakers, with yields and oil lower; Nasdaq and Nvidia also at records. Nothing in the day’s news marked it as the top.

t: 10-year yield 5.365%, the highest since 2002
how: S&P 500 −0.22% to 7,801.77; banks and software fell. A 10-year auction at 5.30% sold well and yields eased later in the day.

t: Banks report: beats and misses are both sold
how: S&P 500 flat at 7,805.45. Goldman lost a 4% pre-market gain after a large beat; Korea’s Kospi fell 5.46% on memory-chip valuations.

t: September CPI: 3.7% over twelve months, up from 3.4%
how: The index move that day was not found. Over the month the odds of a December rate rise went from 50% to 74%.

t: Chips sell off: worst week since June
how: S&P 500 −1.1% to 7,659.44, Nasdaq −2.1%, on doubts about AI borrowing at high yields. On the week the chip fund SMH fell 10.5% while the equal-weight S&P 500 rose 0.5%.

t: Meta −7% after raising its spending range
how: Meta reported after the close on 21 Oct. S&P 500 fund −1.2%, chips −6.7%, and the 10-year yield fell 17bp. The first bounce (7,757.17 on 21 Oct) had failed.

t: Anthropic share-sale filing made public; chips rally
how: Chip stocks rose 8.4% from Monday to Wednesday and the S&P 500 reached 7,743.98 on 28 Oct, just under the 21 Oct high.

t: Fed holds 10–2; both dissenters wanted a rate rise
how: S&P 500 +0.3% to 7,743.98, a fourth straight gain and the second bounce high. Odds of a December rise rose to 85%. Alphabet fell 7% after the bell.

t: Alphabet −12.6%, its worst day; GDP +3.4%
how: Alphabet reported negative free cash flow after the close on 28 Oct. ServiceNow fell 27%. S&P 500 fund −0.4%, Nasdaq-100 fund −1.4%.

t: Intel −28.6%; S&P 500 −1.82%, worst day since June
how: Close 7,580.07; Nasdaq −2.86%, chip index −7.2%. Amazon opened 6% lower despite strong cloud growth. October: Nasdaq −5.3%, Dow +1.7%.

t: US strikes Iranian targets around Hormuz
how: S&P 500 fund −0.5%. Oil had already peaked: US crude fell 13% over the week, from $104.12 to $90.37.

t: Democrats win both chambers of Congress; Dow +3.0%
how: The result came overnight after the 3 Nov vote. Best day after a midterm since 1982; S&P 500 +1.58%. Chips and data-centre stocks already fell. Third bounce high.

t: Data-centre fears: S&P 500 −4.36%, Nasdaq −5.52%
how: Close 7,353.73, the worst day since April 2025; chip index −12%, AMD −17%. The VIX rose 70% to 28.18 and the 10-year yield fell to 4.84%.

t: Payrolls +165,000 against 59,000 expected
how: S&P 500 +0.31% to 7,376.86. The strong number was read as more rate rises. Week: S&P 500 −2.7%, chip index −12.2%.

t: Rebound: S&P 500 +2.35%
how: Nasdaq-100 +3.4% and the VIX fell 22% to 19.92. The start of a three-day bounce that stopped below the 4 Nov level.

t: October CPI above forecast; Waller floats a half-point rise
how: CPI +0.4% in the month, core +0.3% for a third month. S&P 500 −0.38%; the 2-year yield rose 17bp.

t: Bounce high: S&P 500 closes at 7,619.38
how: Up 1.31% with chips +4.8% and the VIX at 17.49. The last up day before seven straight losses.

t: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigns
how: Nvidia opened 12% lower and closed −4.3%. S&P 500 −0.35% to 7,592.40; other chip stocks rose. The 10-year yield reached 5.10%.

t: Producer prices +6.5% on the year; early gains fade
how: S&P 500 −0.40% to 7,561.67 after opening higher. The week was still +2.5%, the best since August. The 10-year yield closed at 5.15%.

t: Nvidia board rules out Huang’s return; S&P 500 −1.92%
how: Close 7,416.59; Nasdaq −2.49%. New limits on chip rentals to Chinese firms; selling spread to banks. The VIX rose 19%.

t: S&P 500 closes below its 5 November low
how: −1.0% to 7,340.53 with 17 of every 20 stocks lower. Home Depot and Disney beat estimates and fell. Nvidia reported after the bell.

t: Nvidia’s strong report is sold; close under the 200-day
how: Results came after the close on 17 Nov. Nvidia rose before the open and ended about 3% lower. S&P 500 −0.23% to 7,323.63, its first close below the 200-day average since 7 April. Fed minutes: almost all officials expect more rises.

t: Anthropic lists; S&P 500 turns +1.3% into −2.02%
how: The index peaked as the record share sale began trading and closed at 7,175.83, with 464 S&P 500 stocks down and 37 up. VIX 28.44. Sixth loss in a row.

t: S&P 500 −3.70% into correction; chip index −10.7%
how: Close 6,910.39, 11.6% below the record; Nasdaq −5.28%, Nvidia −14% on a report of a regulator’s inquiry. The 10-year yield fell to 4.92%; staples rose.
